description: Equate the coefficients of the independent derivative structures obtained in Steps 2 and 3 to determine the constant $a$, ensuring that Grassmann signs from moving $�\eta$ through $�\xi$ and $�\bar{\xi}$ are treated consistently.
reasoning: From Step 2, the scalar kinetic variation contributes coefficients $a$ and $a^*$ multiplying the two independent derivative structures. From Step 3, the fermion kinetic variation contributes $+\sqrt2$ to each corresponding structure, after integration by parts and discarding total derivatives. Since these derivative structures are independent and cannot cancel against the auxiliary-field variation, invariance of the action requires the sum of the scalar and fermion coefficients to vanish separately. Hence $a+\sqrt2=0$ and $a^*+\sqrt2=0$, giving $a=-\sqrt2$. Care must be taken not to introduce an additional erroneous sign when moving $\eta$ or $\bar\eta$ through $\xi$ or $\bar\xi$: the final matching is done only after all expressions have been put into the same canonical Grassmann ordering and spinor-index convention.
result:
The derivative-dependent part of the total variation of the action is, up to surface terms,
$$
\delta_\eta S\big|_{\partial\phi}
=\int d^4x\,\Big[(a+\sqrt2)\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi
+(a^*+\sqrt2)\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi\Big].
$$
The two structures
$$
\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi,
\qquad
\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi
$$
are independent, so their coefficients must vanish separately:
$$
a+\sqrt2=0,
\qquad
a^*+\sqrt2=0.
$$
Therefore
$$
\boxed{a=-\sqrt2},
\qquad
\boxed{a^*=-\sqrt2}.
$$
Thus the scalar variation fixed by cancellation of the derivative terms is
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\phi=-\sqrt2\,\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha}
$$
and its Hermitian conjugate is
$$
\boxed{(\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger=-\sqrt2\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}}.
$$
The Grassmann signs are consistent because all terms have been expressed with the fermionic parameter placed in the same canonical position. In particular, when rewriting dotted contractions such as $(\partial_\mu\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha})\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha}$ as $\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})$, the minus sign from exchanging two Grassmann-odd quantities is compensated by the antisymmetry of the spinor metric used to raise and lower dotted indices.
